etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French parade (“an ostentatious display, a military display”), from parer (“to beautify, prepare, take pride in”) + -ade probably under influence from earlier Italian parata (“preparation, a military parade, an ostentatious display”) and Latin magnō parātū (“with great preparation”). Various senses similarly influenced by earlier French and Italian uses. Doublet of pare.

definitions.definition: (military) Synonym of military parade: A show of troops, an assembly of troops as a show of force, to receive orders, or especially for inspection at set times.

quote.citation: 1642, Henry Hexham, The Principles of Art Military‎[1], volume II, page 31:
quote.text: There is left round about the circuit of the whole quarter, a parallell on all sides some 200, or 250 foote betweene the front of the quarter and the trench, called an Alarme Place, for the souldiers to draw out into Armes, into Parade, or when any Alarme or commotion happens...

quote.text: And from thir Ivorie Port the CherubimForth issuing at th’accustomd hour stood armdTo thir night watches in warlike Parade,When Gabriel to his next in power thus spake...

quote.text: See how the Flow’rs, as at Parade,Under their Colours stand displaid:Each Regiment in order grows,That of the Tulip Pinke and Rose.

quote.text: The next night the soldiers began teaching the girls to dance... Claude saw that a good deal was going on, and he lectured his men at parade. But he realized that he might as well scold at the sparrows.

quote.citation: 1941, George Orwell, The Lion and the Unicorn, Pt. I:
quote.text: A military parade is really a kind of ritual dance, something like a ballet, expressing a certain philosophy of life. The goose-step, for instance, is one of the most horrible sights in the world, far more terrifying than a dive-bomber. It is simply an affirmation of naked power; contained in it, quite consciously and intentionally, is the vision of a boot crashing down on a face. Its ugliness is part of its essence...

definitions.definition: (venery, uncommon) Synonym of gaggle: A group of geese when on the move, particularly a line of goslings shepherded by one or more adults.
(venery, uncommon) Synonym of herd: A group of elephants when on the move.
An organized display of a group of people, particularly
(military, now uncommon) Synonym of parade ground: A place specially designated for such displays or for practicing close-order drills.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French parade (“a parry”), from parer (“to parry, to defend oneself”) + -ade, from Italian parata. Doublet of parry.

definitions.definition: (uncommon) Synonym of parry in both its literal and figurative senses.
